recommendation: Keep this no-change audit commit. If the work group later wants one Provenance record to describe multiple activities, handle that as a new substantive Provenance modeling issue rather than by reapplying this old typo correction.
issue_request: FHIR-7089 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 technical correction for the FHIR-core Provenance opening sentence. The Jira description proposed changing the wording from "activity that created a version of a resource" to "activities that created a version of a resource," and the Jira comment records application in SVN revision 5369.
initial_application: Git commit e734c371bf0fca69d908231da26ff77fc4c27d3d, imported from SVN revision 5369 with subject "#7089 - fix typo," changed source/provenance/provenance-introduction.xml from "information about activity that created" to "information about the activity that created." The applied fix preserved singular activity and added the missing article.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini has an active Provenance resource entry, so source/provenance/provenance-introduction.xml is build-scoped. Later Published/Persuasive issue FHIR-9056 added the current guidance that a Provenance resource corresponds to a single activity and that multiple activities should be represented by independent Provenance records. Searches found no Zulip or Confluence evidence for FHIR-7089 that conflicts with this Jira/source history.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current opening sentence says "the activity that created, revised, deleted, or signed" and is consistent with both the actual FHIR-7089 application and later single-activity Provenance guidance.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive Provenance clarification says multiple activities are recorded as independent Provenance records, supporting the current singular wording.
